summary: Review found six security and data-integrity defects in the drop operation.

findings.summary: Unvalidated state can redirect the destructive Git operation to another directory.
findings.evidence: ENG-25 and ENG-26: folder comes from state.json's spec_dir rather than the discovered state path. A sandbox run with spec_dir set to src successfully committed deletion of src/factory/valuable.txt while reporting success; the archive contained the actual run folder instead.
findings.fix: Derive the removal path from the discovered run folder and validate state identity against that path before any filesystem or Git operation.

findings.summary: Untracked design files are committed and automatically pushed.
findings.evidence: ENG-25: git mv moves the design directory, then git add stages its entire destination. A sandbox run with an untracked design/secret.txt included that file in the drop commit. The PR workflow subsequently pushes the commit, potentially publishing local secrets.
findings.fix: Stage only tracked design evidence being moved; archive untracked files without adding them to the commit.

findings.summary: Rollback destroys pre-existing uncommitted changes in the run folder.
findings.evidence: ENG-26: when git rm refuses a locally modified tracked file, the exception handler checks out the entire folder from HEAD and deletes the verified archive. In a sandbox, modified brief.md reverted to its committed contents and the only archive was removed.
findings.fix: Refuse before mutation when affected tracked files have local changes, or preserve and restore their exact working-tree and index contents on failure.

findings.summary: Archive filtering silently discards every nested file named lock.json.
findings.evidence: ENG-26: ignore_patterns applies recursively, and verification uses the same recursive exclusion. A sandbox run containing evidence/lock.json succeeded while deleting that file from the worktree and omitting it from the archive; only the root transient lock was meant to be excluded.
findings.fix: Exclude only the run folder's root lock.json and verify all nested files.

findings.summary: Archive copying follows repository-controlled symlinks outside the run folder.
findings.evidence: ENG-25 and ENG-24: copytree defaults to dereferencing symlinks, without checking their targets or bounding copied data. A tracked symlink to an external secret was archived as a regular file containing the secret. A directory symlink can likewise copy an external tree into the archive.
findings.fix: Preserve symlinks without following them, or reject links whose resolved targets escape the run folder; verify link identity rather than dereferenced contents.

findings.summary: The run lock is released before removal and commit complete.
findings.evidence: ENG-23 and ENG-26: another process can acquire the run lock or add an artifact after archive verification but before the final rmtree. A sandbox injection at lock release created a late artifact that was absent from both archive and worktree after successful drop.
findings.fix: Hold the run lock through the complete destructive operation and ensure changes cannot be removed after the verified snapshot.
